label: Individuated veracity truth and negation interpretation
term: world-indexed truth and interpreted content negation
definition: Reuse of Semantics World Content: trueAt assigns truth to an individuated content at a world; neg maps contents to their represented negations, with the explicit truth condition trueAt w (neg c) iff not trueAt w c. Content and World are arbitrary types. Contents with the same truth conditions need not be identical. Actual world designation is an explicit parameter, not a theorem of metaphysical possibility.
note: The primitive truth interpretation and content identity require external interpretation; the structure supplies only classical negation semantics. No relation between semantic equivalence and identity, cognition, historical utterance or epistemic access is assumed. See docs/notes/divine-veracity-1410.md, Individuated-content continuation.
